extracted.intended_audience: U.S. policymakers (Congress, Secretary of the Interior), Bureau of Indian Affairs, tribal leaders and advocates
extracted.subtask_description: Recommendations and standards for extending full federal recognition to landless Indian tribes and for restructuring the Bureau of Indian Affairs, Indian Claims Commission awards, funding, and related trust responsibilities. Focused on concrete institutional, legal, and administrative changes to protect tribal rights and re-establish tribal land bases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Congressional directive to extend full federal recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: THE CONGRESS OF THE UNITED STATES DIRECT THE PRIMARY AGENT OF THE TRUSTEE/THE SECRETARY OF THE INTERIOR TO IMMEDIATELY EXTEND FULL FEDERAL RECOGNITION TO THOSE INDIAN TRIBES, GROUPS OR BANDS WITH WHOM A LEGAL RELATIONSHIP EXISTS DUE TO TREATY, ACT OF CONGRESS, EXECUTIVE ORDER, ADMINISTRATIVE DECISION, INDIAN CLAIMS COMMISSION OR JUDICIAL DECREE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendation asks Congress to instruct the Secretary to extend recognition where a legal relationship already exists; intended to remedy historic omissions and to halt selective recognition policies that exclude landless tribes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Case-by-case review using established, well-defined criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: THAT THE SECRETARY MAKE A FULL CASE-BY-CASE REVIEW BASED ON AN ESTABLISHED AND WELL DEFINED CRITERIA FOR RECOGNITION BASED ON ETHNOLOGICAL, HISTORICAL, LEGAL AND POLITICAL FINDINGS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires the Secretary to use objective multidisciplinary criteria (ethnological, historical, legal, political) in recognition determinations; implies transparent, documented findings per case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate provision of fiduciary protections after recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: THAT THE SECRETARY ONCE MAKING A DETERMINATION TO EXTEND FULL FEDERAL RECOGNITION TO A TRIBE THEN IMMEDIATELY COMMENCE TO PROVIDE FOR THE PROTECTION AND THE FULFILLMENT OF THE FIDUCIARY RELATIONSHIP, AS REQUESTED BY THESE TRIBES.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognition must be accompanied by prompt execution of fiduciary duties—service provision, protection of rights, trust responsibilities—rather than delayed implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek increased allocations so services are not reduced elsewhere
rubrics_metrics.description: THAT IN EXTENDING FULL FEDERAL RECOGNITION TO THESE TRIBES, THAT THE SECRETARY WILL SEEK FROM CONGRESS AN INCREASE IN THE ALLOCATIONS TO THOSE AGENCIES WHICH ARE CURRENTLY PROVIDING SERVICES TO INDIAN TRIBES SO THAT NO SERVICES TO OTHER TRIBES ARE REDUCED.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognition should be funded through additional appropriations rather than reallocations that would reduce services to already-recognized tribes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide trust lands for tribal needs and exclusive use
rubrics_metrics.description: THAT THE SECRETARY SHALL ALSO PROVIDE FOR SUCH TRUST LANDS AS MAY BE REQUIRED FOR THE NEED AND EXCLUSIVE USE OF THESE LANDLESS TRIBES.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit recommendation that recognition include provision of a land base held in trust by the federal government to affirm tribal status and enable tribal survival and governance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modify Indian Claims Commission awards to allow land and tribal-approved plans
rubrics_metrics.description: THAT THE INDIAN CLAIMS COMMISSION AWARDS BE MODIFIED BY CONGRESS TO REFLECT TRIBAL ATTITUDES IN INDIAN COUNTRY, TO PROVIDE LAND AS WELL AS MONETARY PAYMENT FOR TRIBAL CLAIMS TO BE DISALLOWED OR UTILIZED ACCORDING TO A TRIBALLY APPROVED PLAN.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rejects rigid per-capita monetary distributions; calls for ICC awards to permit land awards or fund land purchase/tribal plans per tribal preferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bureau provide technical assistance to re-establish land base and funds for tribal government
rubrics_metrics.description: THAT THE BUREAU PROVIDE TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE TO LANDLESS TRIBES IN RE-ESTABLISHING A LAND BASE FOR EACH TRIBE AND PROVIDE THE NECESSARY FUNDS FOR OPERATION AND ADMINISTRATION OF THE TRIBAL GOVERNMENT.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes capacity-building support (technical and financial) rather than external management; tribes assert desire to manage their own affairs and request assistance focused on enabling self-government.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis on assistance, not Bureau management of tribal affairs
rubrics_metrics.description: WE ARE INTENT UPON MANAGING OUR OWN AFFAIRS AND WOULD THEREFORE REGARD ANY EFFORT OF THE BUREAU TO MANAGE OUR AFFAIRS AS UNDUE INTERFERENCE INTO THE SELF-GOVERNING RESPONSIBILITIES OF THE TRIBE. IT IS IN THIS CONTEXT THAT WE EMPHASIZE THE NEED FOR SIA CONCENTRATION ON TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE RATHER THAN MANAGEMENT.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guides Bureau behavior: provide tools, training, funds, and advice but avoid paternalistic management or takeover of tribal governance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal capability to protect Indian rights and tax exemptions
rubrics_metrics.description: LEGAL CAPABILITY TO PROTECT ALL INDIAN RIGHTS TO FISH, WATER, AND LAND RESOURCES AS WELL AS EXEMPTION FROM STATE TAXATION FOR ALL INDIANS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calls for federal legal support and statutory/regulatory measures ensuring tribes can protect treaty/resource rights and obtain state tax exemptions where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organize the Bureau to include tribal participation
rubrics_metrics.description: THAT THE BUREAU BE ORGANIZED SO AS TO INCLUDE THE TRIBES. THIS CAPABILITY SHOULD BE WITHIN THE BUREAU, INDEPENDENT OF THE DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND JUSTICE DEPARTMENT.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structural reform: create governance mechanisms within the Bureau that formally include tribal representatives in organization and decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make the Bureau independent of the Department of the Interior (administratively under Congress)
rubrics_metrics.description: THAT THE BUREAU BE INDEPENDENT OF THE DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR, FREE FROM THE CONFLICTS OF INTERESTS OF THAT DEPARTMENT. IT WOULD BE OF GREATER USE TO INDIANS IF THE BUREAU FUNCTIONED ADMINISTRATIVELY UNDER THE CONGRESS AND WAS NOT A POLITICAL 'FOOTBALL'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocates removing the Bureau from Interior Department control to reduce conflicts and politicization; suggests administrative placement under Congress for stability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure Bureau to encourage perpetual Indian participation in policy-making
rubrics_metrics.description: THAT THE BUREAU BE STRUCTURED TO ENCOURAGE * * PERPETUAL INDIAN PARTICIPATION IN BUREAU POLICY-MAKING. INDIANS HAVE BEEN TOO LONG TOLD HOW TO ARRANGE THEIR AFFAIRS RATHER THAN ALLOWED TO ACTIVELY INITIATE EFFORTS ON THEIR OWN BEHALF.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutionalize ongoing, meaningful tribal involvement in Bureau policy decisions at all levels rather than ad hoc consultation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Increase Bureau accessibility and locate facilities closer to people
rubrics_metrics.description: THAT THE BUREAU BE MORE ACCESSIBLE TO INDIANS AND SHOULD BE BY LOCATING ITS FACILITIES CLOSER TO THE PEOPLE IT SERVES WITHOUT REDUCING THE CURRENT LEVEL OF SERVICES.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decentralize physical presence so local offices are near tribal communities; maintain service levels while reducing distance barriers to access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decentralize authority: empower local offices and eliminate area office layer
rubrics_metrics.description: LOCAL OFFICES SHOULD BE NEAR OUR PEOPLE; THE LOCAL OFFICE SHOULD HAVE DIRECT AUTHORITY FROM THE NATIONAL OFFICE AND THE AREA OFFICE SHOULD BE ELIMINATED. THIS WOULD PROVIDE THE LOCAL OFFICE DIRECT ABILITY TO GAIN AUTHORIZATION FOR LOCAL EFFORTS AS DEFINED BY THE TRIBES. ELIMINATION OF THE AREA OFFICE WOULD ALSO REPRESENT A MAJOR ADMINISTRATIVE SAVING WHILE INCREASING THE BUREAU'S ABILITY TO DIRECTLY SERVE INDIANS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational recommendation to streamline bureaucracy: remove intermediate area offices, grant local offices direct authorization and closer ties to tribes for responsiveness and cost savings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overhaul Bureau regulations and guidelines for flexibility via a Task Force
rubrics_metrics.description: THAT THE BUREAU HAVE REGULATIONS AND GUIDELINES OVERHAULED TO REFLECT GREAT FLEXIBILITY IN DEALING WITH THE DIVERSE INTERESTS OF INDIANS. THIS COULD BE ACCOMPLISHED BY A CONGRESSIONALLY ESTABLISHED TASK FORCE INCLUDING INDIANS FROM ALL AREAS OF INDIAN COUNTRY WITH SPECIFIC AUTHORIZATION TO RE-WRITE THE BUREAU'S REGULATIONS AND GUIDELINES. NON-INDIANS SHOULD BE INCLUDED AS THEIR SKILLS WARRANT.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calls for participatory regulatory reform: a congressionally-mandated task force (including tribal and qualified non-tribal expertise) to modernize BIA rules for flexibility across diverse tribal circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consolidate essential services under a separate independent agency
rubrics_metrics.description: THAT THE CONGRESS CONSOLIDATE ALL ESSENTIAL SERVICES FOR INDIANS AND INDIAN TRIBES UNDER A SEPARATE INDEPENDENT AGENCY WHICH WILL BE RESPONSIVE TO THE NEEDS OF INDIAN PEOPLE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocates centralization (consolidation) of Indian services in an independent entity distinct from current departmental structures to improve responsiveness and accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modify Indian Claims Commission scope and longevity
rubrics_metrics.description: THE LIFE OF THE INDIAN CLAIMS COMMISSION IS TOO SHORT; IT NEEDS TO HEAR OTHER TYPES OF CLAIMS OTHER THAN LAND ISSUES.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend extending the Commission's mandate (and likely its duration) and expanding the range of claim types it can adjudicate beyond land-only issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honor Snyder Act authorization: Bureau must serve non-reservation Indians
rubrics_metrics.description: THE BUREAU OF INDIAN AFFAIRS HAS CONSISTENTLY EXCLUDED INDIANS WHO DO NOT LIVE ON INDIAN RESERVATIONS FROM ITS SERVICE POPULATION. THE LANDLESS TRIBES HAVE BEEN NOTABLY EXCLUDED FROM BUREAU CONSIDERATION IN SPITE OF A SPECIFIC AUTHORIZATION THROUGH THE SNYDER ACT WHICH REQUIRES THAT THE BUREAU OF INDIAN AFFAIRS ASSIST INDIANS THROUGHOUT THE UNITED STATES.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandates that Bureau interpret and implement Snyder Act authority to include landless and non-reservation Indians in its service population, ensuring health, education, and employment services are extended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use negotiated bilateral term trust agreements after recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursue a bilateral, negotiated trust agreement with the tribe that would spell out in fairly clear detail, over a period of time, the kinds of assistance the United States would be prepared to provide to that tribe, at what particular time, the kinds of work that would be undertaken to insure that the tribe had a land base of its own.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Testimony recommends statutory or regulatory requirement that recognition be followed by a term trust agreement (with timelines, deliverables, land plans) negotiated between the U.S. and tribe to ensure orderly restoration and capacity development.
